problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\,y(2)=e
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method. What entry should be placed in the column for $Δy$ in the second row of the table below if the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}?$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $e$ | $8$ | $4$ |
| $$ | $$ | $$ | $\,?\,$ |
worked_solution:
To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =2+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =e+4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $e$ | $8$ | $4$ |
| $\frac{5}{2}$ | $e+4$ | $$ | $$ |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule (using the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row), and we compute 
$Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =4x\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\  & =4(\frac{5}{2})\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4) \\  & =10\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4) \\ Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =10\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4)\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4)\end{aligned}
$$

 

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $e$ | $8$ | $4$ |
| $\frac{5}{2}$ | $e+4$ | $10\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4)$ | $5\operatorname{ln}⁡(e+4)$ |
